newsitem.title: UK: Railtrack off after Prescott comments.
newsitem.headline: Railtrack off after Prescott comments.

text.p: Shares in Railtrack Plc, Britain's rail network operator, stumbled on Friday amid fears of harsh treatment from the newly-elected Labour government, dealers said.
By 0923 GMT, the shares were off 13-1/2p to 644-1/2, reversing gains made on Thursday after the group posted strong profits.
Deputy Prime Minister John Prescott on Thursday indicated the company faced tougher treatment that could come in the form of windfall taxes, fines and tougher sanctions
"There's no doubt they could tighten the regulatory framework, which could damage profitability, and it's an obvious whipping boy," said one dealer.
Yet earlier SBC Warburg raised its 1998 earnings estimate, by eight percent to 362 million stg, but maintained its "sell" recommendation on Railtrack, dealers said.
The analyst at SBC Warburg couldn't immediately be reached for comment.
